processing: Certified organic orthodox Darjeeling black tea, withered, rolled, oxidised and dried in the traditional way.
harvest_season: First flush in spring and second flush in early summer are the lots seen for sale.
appearance_dry: Twisted Darjeeling leaf in mixed olive and brown, as usual for the region.
appearance_liquor: Pale gold in first flush, amber in second flush.
taste_profile: Little is recorded for this garden alone. Expect the general Darjeeling pattern: floral and brisk in spring, fruitier and fuller in summer.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western-style, as for other Darjeeling. Use cooler water and a shorter steep for first flush.

vintage_note: Sold by year and flush; first and second flush lots from 2026 are on the market. Spellings vary between sellers, so search under Nurbong, Noorbong and Norbung.
description:
Nurbong is an organic garden in the Kurseong area of Darjeeling. Sellers spell it three ways, which is the first thing to know when looking for it.

The garden is listed in the same organic group as Ambootia. The tea is made in the orthodox way, so the season does most to set the character of the lot.

In the cup, expect what is typical of Darjeeling: light and floral in spring, fuller in summer. Few independent tasting notes exist, so treat this as a starting point.

Look for the year, the flush and an organic certification on the bag.
history: Little is documented about when Nurbong was founded or who planted it. It appears in lists of Darjeeling's organic gardens and in the holdings of Darjeeling Organic Tea Estates under the spelling Noorbong.
